posts.title: The Download: Anthropic’s IPO, smarter power grids, and exercise pills
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Will the real Anthropic please stand up? After weeks of frenzied speculation, Anthropic has filed its IPO prospectus. The 335-page document (100 pages or so are focused on risks) lays out…
bullets: Anthropic has officially filed its IPO prospectus, a 335-page document that highlights the company's internal tensions between its AI safety mission and its profit-driven commercial objectives.
The filing is expected to serve as a bellwether for the broader AI investment boom, testing market appetite for companies balancing high-risk, high-reward research with massive capital requirements.

Beyond AI, the report highlights emerging developments in solid-state transformers to address grid capacity constraints and medical research into 'exercise pills' designed to mimic the physiological benefits of physical activity for those with chronic illnesses.

posts.title: Anthropic S-1, The Cost of Compute, Who Is Paying?
posts.summary: Anthropic's IPO is finally here; the core business is very profitable, but competition may eat all of the profits, even as investors are set up for endless dilution.
bullets: Anthropic’s S-1 filing reveals a business model that is currently profitable at the core, highlighting the potential for AI-native companies to generate significant revenue.
The long-term sustainability of these profits is threatened by intense market competition, which risks commoditizing AI services and eroding margins.
Investors face the prospect of significant and potentially endless dilution as the company continues to navigate the massive capital requirements of AI compute infrastructure.
The filing underscores the tension between the high operational costs of training and running large models and the necessity of maintaining a competitive pricing strategy in a crowded landscape.

posts.title: The imec Report: Scaling Optical Interconnects For The AI Era
posts.summary:
Unprecedented demand for bandwidth calls for bringing optics closer to silicon through a fundamental rethinking of the optical interconnect roadmap.
The post The imec Report: Scaling Optical Interconnects For The AI Era appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Copper-based electrical interconnects are reaching fundamental physical limits, where power consumption and thermal constraints hinder the scaling of next-generation AI systems.
Optical interconnects are identified as the critical path forward, offering superior energy efficiency and signal integrity over longer distances compared to traditional electrical links.

Imec emphasizes that achieving multi-terabit-per-second interfaces requires moving optics closer to silicon, transitioning from pluggable transceivers to integration directly within the package and wafer stack.

posts.title: Analog Superposition Increases Effective PCM Storage Density (IBM Research Europe)
posts.summary:
Researchers at IBM Research Europe published “Superposed analog memory for vector storage in neural networks.” Summary: Researchers demonstrated an analog phase-change memory architecture that stores multiple AI vectors in superposition, increasing effective storage density with a tunable accuracy tradeoff. Tests on prototype PCM hardware showed inference accuracy close to full-precision software. Find the technical paper here.... » read more
The post Analog Superposition Increases Effective PCM Storage Density (IBM Research Europe) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: IBM Research Europe has demonstrated an analog phase-change memory (PCM) architecture that stores multiple AI vectors in superposition to boost effective storage density.
The approach allows for a tunable accuracy tradeoff, enabling developers to balance memory capacity against the precision requirements of specific neural network workloads.
Prototype hardware testing confirms that this superposed storage method achieves inference accuracy levels comparable to full-precision software implementations.

posts.title: VW considers bringing Xpeng co-developed architecture to European models, report says
posts.summary:
The proposal would cover about 75% of next-generation models from Volkswagen, Skoda and Cupra, pending review by group management.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Volkswagen is evaluating a proposal to adopt its China-developed electrical/electronic architecture (CEA) for European models, potentially covering 75% of future vehicles from the VW, Skoda, and Cupra brands.
Internal estimates suggest that shifting to the Xpeng-co-developed architecture could save the group between €4 billion and €5 billion in development costs.

The potential move creates internal friction regarding the company's software strategy, as it could diminish the role of the existing $5.8 billion partnership with Rivian and introduce technical risks related to European regulatory adaptation.
